purpose: How many LIVE canary attestations this repository must retain. Zero live canaries must not read as 'all clean': /.agent-harness/runs/ is gitignored wholesale and canary directories are force-added one at a time, so a checkout that misses them found nothing and reported ok -- the detector's own default was fail-open (round-10 finding). Declaring the number turns absence into an error. A tree that legitimately holds no canary evidence, such as a synthetic test fixture, simply has no policy file; check_canary_freshness.py then requires none, refuses a policy file that git tracks but the working tree has lost, and refuses one that exists but git does not track, so the declaration cannot be removed or replaced to silence the floor.
why_two: Raised from 1 at D-070 Part B20, on a round-13 registered reviewer's finding (F-R13-006). Two live canaries now discharge DIFFERENT named obligations -- C8 is the overlapping-run pointer bracket for D-065 obligation 4, and C9 is the 24-way concurrent-stop race for obligation 1 plus the live Start-failure measurement for obligation 2. Under a floor of 1 the reviewer deleted C9's entire run directory with no tampering at all and the checker still reported ok, because a minimum is a minimum and C8 alone satisfied it. That is correct behaviour for the rule as written and wrong for what the evidence is FOR: losing C9 loses the only executed evidence for two obligations while the harness reports clean. The floor counts unique ids rather than files, so this cannot be satisfied by duplicating one canary.
known_limitation: This is a COUNT, not a manifest: it cannot require that C8 and C9 specifically survive, only that two unique receipt-backed tracked canaries do. Naming required ids here would be the stronger form and is deliberately not done yet, because a required-id list must be maintained by hand and a stale entry would block every commit until someone edited it -- the same failure mode as the written rules that killed four earlier canaries. Recorded as a stated limit rather than silently closed.
